# Oska checker report

## Diagnostic codes

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `E0200` | Unknown name "x" with a \\ in it, as in `Strng`. See [the tour](#tour). | Replace the name with the closest one. |
| `E0201` | A trait <script>alert(1)</script> where a type is expected. Then more. | None. |
| `E0140` | An or-pattern such as `A \| B`. | None: write one arm each. |

### Examples

#### `E0200`

```oska error=E0200
fn f(x: Strng) {}
```

```oska fixed=E0200
fn f(x: String) {}
```

#### `E0201`

```oska error=E0201
fn show(x: Display) {
    let note = "<b>\"quoted\"</b>"
}

```

```text
not an example
| `E0999` | Not a code row. | None. |
```

# Oska runtime

## Panics

| Code | Panic |
| --- | --- |
| `P0004` | Division by zero, see [Tests](#tests). Spans the operation. |

---

Source: https://oskalang.dev/codes/

# Error codes

Every diagnostic code Oska reports, with a program that fails with it and the same program fixed. `oskac explain <code>` prints an entry offline.

All of them are in [codes.json](https://oskalang.dev/codes.json) as data.

- [E0200](https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0200.md): Unknown name "x" with a \\ in it, as in `Strng`
- [E0201](https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0201.md): A trait <script>alert(1)</script> where a type is expected
- [E0140](https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0140.md): An or-pattern such as `A | B`
- [P0004](https://oskalang.dev/codes/P0004.md): Division by zero, see [Tests](runtime.md#tests)

---

Source: https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0200.html

# E0200

Unknown name "x" with a \\ in it, as in `Strng`. See [the tour](/checker.md#tour).

**Machine-applicable fix:** Replace the name with the closest one.

## Example

This program fails with `E0200`.

```oska
fn f(x: Strng) {}
```

## Fixed

The same program, fixed.

```oska
fn f(x: String) {}
```

Listed in the [checker notes](/checker.md#e0200). `oskac explain E0200` prints this entry offline.

---

Source: https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0201.html

# E0201

A trait <script>alert(1)</script> where a type is expected. Then more.

**Machine-applicable fix:** none.

## Example

This program fails with `E0201`.

```oska
fn show(x: Display) {
    let note = "<b>\"quoted\"</b>"
}

```

Listed in the [checker notes](/checker.md#e0201). `oskac explain E0201` prints this entry offline.

---

Source: https://oskalang.dev/codes/E0140.html

# E0140

An or-pattern such as `A | B`.

**Machine-applicable fix:** none.

Listed in the [checker notes](/checker.md). `oskac explain E0140` prints this entry offline.

---

Source: https://oskalang.dev/codes/P0004.html

# P0004

Division by zero, see [Tests](/runtime.md#tests). Spans the operation.

**Machine-applicable fix:** none.

Listed in the [runtime notes](/runtime.md). `oskac explain P0004` prints this entry offline.
